items.headline: US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation
items.blurb: Nvidia's share price have fallen 7% as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's reinstatement.
items.text: US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation. Blanche said he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback. Huang was given his job back less than two weeks after being forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Asked several times on Tuesday if the justice department or FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche responded: "I don't know what you're talking about." Huang is still set to appear before Congress next week, where he will be questioned about national security concerns over his relationship with an alleged China spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia. The US commerce department has also announced it was preparing to blacklist the tech company Megaspeed, which has been suspected of helping to divert advanced chips to China. items.headline: French ex-President Sarkozy and wife Carla Bruni to face trial
items.blurb: It is the latest case involving Nicolas Sarkozy who became the first French ex-president to go to jail last year.
items.text: Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife Carla Bruni-Sarkozy are to face trial next year over charges stemming from the former French president's conviction for conspiring to fund his election campaign with money from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi. The charges centre on the retraction of the testimony of a key witness who had initially said he had evidence that could incriminate Sarkozy. Sarkozy was given a five-year sentence in the case last September and became the first French ex-president to go to jail, even though he only spent 20 days behind bars. He has always denied doing anything wrong in the case and the appeals verdict is expected next Monday. Since losing his re-election bid in 2012, Sarkozy has faced several criminal investigations. In 2024, he was handed a one-year sentence – of which six months were suspended – over the illegal financing of his 2012 re-election campaign. items.headline: Alaska ends deal to give voter records to US Justice Department
items.blurb: The decision follows the conclusion of the 2026 midterm elections and an effort under Trump to gather state voter rolls.
items.text: Alaska has terminated a memorandum of understanding that granted the United States Department of Justice (DOJ) access to the state’s voter rolls. On Monday, outgoing Lieutenant Governor Nancy Dahlstrom, who oversees the state’s elections, announced she had notified the Justice Department that Alaska was withdrawing from the 2025 memo, effective immediately. In a statement, Dahlstrom said her state had entered the agreement “in good faith to cooperate with our federal law enforcement partners”. But she acknowledged a shift had taken place after the 2026 midterm elections. “The circumstances have now changed,” Dahlstrom wrote. “The election has concluded and the agreement no longer serves a continuing purpose.” The reversal comes after months of pressure from the administration of President Donald Trump for states to surrender their voter rolls to federal authorities. Trump has argued that such information was necessary to root out fraud during the November 3 midterms. But officials in certain states argued that the federal government was encroaching on their constitutional authority. Under the US Constitution, only states have the power to administer elections. items.text: One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has said the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK. Saurav Das said he was meant to board a flight on Tuesday morning but was told by immigration officers his passport had been "flagged" because of discrepancies involving his date of birth. In an interview with the BBC, Das said there were no discrepancies in his documents, accusing the Indian government of using cheap tactics to stop activists from travelling and speaking on issues that matter to young people. The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment. Saurav told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme the incident showed the government was "scared". "They are scared of the cockroach movement. They're scared of young people asking them questions because they have never had to deal with a generation that wants to ask questions so head on. So that jitters them." items.headline: Rebel group retreats in DR Congo after heavy clashes with government forces
items.blurb: CRP halts advance towards Bunia, citing commitments made during Ugandan-mediated talks with government.
items.text: The rebel group led by convicted war criminal Thomas Lubanga has withdrawn from areas recently seized in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) after days of heavy fighting with government forces. The Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) announced on Tuesday that it had decided to halt an advance towards the town of Bunia, the capital of Ituri province in northeast DRC. In a statement, the group cited a commitment made in talks with the Congolese government, mediated by Uganda’s President Yoweri Museveni, as one of the reasons for its withdrawal. The CRP’s decision came one day after the group seized the Iga-Barriere, a strategic area about 25km north of Bunia, forcing government troops to withdraw towards the provincial capital. Lubanga, a former leader of the Union of Congolese Patriots, was convicted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in 2012 on charges of recruiting and using child soldiers. He was sentenced to 14 years in prison and released in March 2020 after completing his sentence. Lubanga remains sanctioned by the United Nations. Lubanga announced the formation of the CRP

items.blurb: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the…
items.text: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government. Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, triggering the explosion, the officials told the Associated Press. Satellite imagery showed the Merkury had sunk after the attack, which took place in the Mediterranean, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine , marking a notable geographic expansion of the now near five-year war. items.headline: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
items.blurb: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.
items.text: Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark case in the US. In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage. Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation. In a statement, Huawei said the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years". Jurors in a Brooklyn court found Huawei guilty of 10 out of 12 counts, which included conspiracy to violate US sanctions. However, the jury declined to convict Huawei of the racketeering conspiracy charge, which required members to find the firm acted like a criminal enterprise. items.text: The Judicial Magistrate of the Special Court for POCSO (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences) Cases in Tirunelveli, Suresh Kumar, has been placed under suspension over allegations of misconduct. Sources in Tirunelveli District Court said Mr. Suresh Kumar was facing allegations of misconduct when he was serving at the Mettupalayam Court in 2016. Following an inquiry conducted by the Madras High Court into these allegations, the suspension order was served on Mr. Suresh Kumar on Monday (November 23, 2026) night. Consequently, he did not attend court on Tuesday (November 24), the sources said. items.headline: Meity revises ‘Made in India’ rules for govt IT hardware purchases
items.blurb: India’s new government procurement rules reward local R&D, design and chip manufacturing, not just assembly, to boost domestic value addition.
items.text: The ministry of electronics and information technology (Meity) has changed how laptops, desktops, servers and other IT hardware are judged as ‘Made in India’ for government purchases. Companies will now get more weightage for research, design and chip-level work done in the country, not just assembly. Under government procurement rules, buyers give preference to suppliers whose products meet set local content thresholds. Those suppliers are classified as Class-I or Class-II local suppliers. The new notification decides how that local content is counted. The rules cover central government purchases. They also cover purchases by states and local bodies under schemes fully or partly funded by the Centre. The notification, dated November 20 and setting a six-month deadline for the new rules to come into effects, sets out a new method for calculating local content in six products: desktop and all-in-one PCs, laptops, thin clients (low-cost terminals that rely on a central server for computing), servers, computer monitors and interactive flat panel displays (IFPDs), which are smart boards used in classrooms and offices. items.text: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) downplayed an alleged clash between two senior Indian Police Service officers at a party as a “personal fight”. The incident, involving a Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) and a Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), occurred at an Assam Police battalion in the western part of the State on Sunday night (November 22, 2026). “There was a fight between two persons at a private programme. We have nothing to do here, as it was personal and had no connection with the Police Department. Sometimes, we also end up having arguments,” the Chief Minister told journalists on the sidelines of an official event. “We would have done something had it happened during official duty. I have no comment on a personal matter,” he said. According to reports, the DIG in question was among several senior police officers invited to a party the SSP had organised. items.blurb: Samajwadi Party's first list of five candidates was announced on Tuesday, naming nominees for constituencies across Saharanpur, Shamli, Amroha and Lalitpur.
items.text: The Samajwadi Party on Tuesday night announced its first list of five candidates for the upcoming 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election, naming nominees for constituencies in Saharanpur, Shamli, Amroha and Lalitpur. The first list comprises four Muslims and one non-Yadav OBC candidate. Nahid Hasan had won three successive elections on the seat - in the 2014 bypolls, 2017, then 2022 polls. Umar Ali is the sitting SP MLA from Behat, while Ashu Malik is the sitting SP MLA from Saharanpur assembly seat. Mahboob Ali is also the sitting SP MLA from Amroha and has won the seat five consecutive times till 2022. Lalitpur is the only seat in the list that is not currently with the SP. BJP won the seat in 2017 and 2022. Ahead of the announcement, SP president Akhilesh Yadav had signalled that seat-sharing discussions with the Congress were progressing smoothly, saying the two parties had made a beginning with '26 winnable seats' and would continue negotiations together. items.headline: Households braced for soaring energy bills with new price cap to be announced
items.blurb: Domestic gas prices will rise significantly in January under regulator Ofgem's new price cap.
items.text: Domestic energy bills are expected to soar in January for millions of households, with regulator Ofgem to announce the precise increase shortly. A typical annual bill is predicted to rise by 26% in the new year, according to consultancy Cornwall Insight, in a forecast made ahead of the official announcement. Ofgem's new cap, which sets a maximum price for each unit of energy, will come into force at the coldest time of year. Customers pay for what they use and charities and suppliers expect debt to rise and a wave of people to need emergency support. The government will make a £100 payment to millions of households to help cover winter costs, in addition to an ongoing VAT cut on electricity. The warm home discount will also take £150 off bills for six million households on benefits this winter. There have been calls for this support, funded through everyone's bill, to be extended. Effectively, APL Apollo will shoulder most of the debt burden for Tata Steel’s ₹ 32,265-crore takeover, investors argued. The promoter will exit at ₹ 2,100 per share, while the shareholders will be left holding a stock that traded at ₹ 1,668.15 on the BSE on Monday after a sell-off wiped out more than a fifth of APL Apollo's value. At least one mutual fund manager and one proxy advisory firm told Mint that they were against the transaction. "This deal is unfair to minority shareholders of APL Apollo Tubes because APL Apollo is buying Tata Steel's assets at huge valuations while also funding the promoter Sanjay Gupta family exit at atrocious valuations," said Shriram Subramanian, managing director of proxy advisory firm InGovern. items.blurb: Shadowfax Technologies has agreed to acquire select business assets of WeFast India and technology and intellectual property (IP) rights associated with Borzo for $2.5 million (approximately Rs 23.3 crore) as the logistics company expands into on-demand intra-city goods transportation.
items.text: Shadowfax Technologies has agreed to acquire select business assets of WeFast India and technology and intellectual property (IP) rights associated with Borzo for $2.5 million (approximately Rs 23.3 crore) as the logistics company expands into on-demand intra-city goods transportation. The transaction involves two separate agreements. Shadowfax will acquire technology, software and related IP rights in India from Incrin Limited for $2 million, along with a licence for the BORZO trademark for $50,000. Under a separate agreement, Shadowfax will purchase identified business assets of Wefast India Private Limited for $450,000 in Indian rupees. These include contracts, equipment, domain names, databases and related technology. The agreement also provides for the transfer of identified employees. The transactions are subject to customary conditions precedent and are expected to be completed by March 31, 2027. If you thought the machine might have won, you are wrong. The man, named Viswanathan Anand, beat Fritz. The computer had white pieces and it opted for the Spanish Game. Anand, who hadn’t yet won any of his World titles yet, played the Berlin Defence. It is a solid option when you are playing with black pieces. And it was Berlin Defence that D. Gukesh opted for the opening game of his World chess championship match against Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva on Tuesday. The chess world had indeed been curious about the opening in the first game of the widely anticipated match between the 20-year-olds. Sindarov began by pushing the pawn in front of him by two squares, to which Gukesh replied with a similar move. Just seven moves later, the queens were off the board, and a draw would become the likeliest result later on. And it was draw.

items.headline: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?

items.text: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It’s too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There’s not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. items.headline: Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization
items.blurb: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network. Now, agentic AI is adding to the load.
items.text: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network . Now, agentic AI is adding to the load. Tasks conducted by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers. As AI inference shifts from hyperscale training clouds—the huge centralized data centers where raw AI models ingest vast datasets and learn—to real-time, latency-sensitive applications, the need for on-premises or near-premises infrastructure grows. As a result, the gap between enterprise networks that are ready to support AI and those that are not is widening. As few as half of enterprises believe their current networks can handle AI’s bandwidth and latency demands, according to a recent study . This report explores how treating network modernization as an on-going strategy rather than a one-off project can help organizations adapt in the face of disruption and uncertainty. items.headline: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.blurb: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
items.text: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. items.headline: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
items.blurb: As millions embrace personal AI assistants, a new benchmark reveals that even the most advanced AI models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without introducing potential new problems.
items.text: AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But new research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives. According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences. ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them. items.text: Sarvam AI has launched Sarvam Dictate, an API that lets developers integrate voice dictation in English and 22 Indian languages, priced at ₹0.50 per minute of audio Sarvam’s launch, alongside Murf AI’s new speech-to-text model Finch, shows growing competition among Indian AI startups to power multilingual voice applications for businesses Sarvam claims Dictate required 40% fewer character edits than Gemini 3.5 Transcribe for short English dictations and 47% fewer across Indian languages and Hinglish in its tests AI unicorn Sarvam AI has launched Sarvam Dictate, an API that lets developers add voice dictation in English and 22 Indian languages to their applications. Priced at ₹0.50 per minute of audio, the service combines speech recognition with transcript editing in a single API call. It is designed to turn spoken inputs into text for messages, documents, and business records. Dictate pairs the startup’s Saaras V4 speech recognition model with a version of its Sarvam 105B large language model trained for dictation. items.headline: Sarvam Vs Critics, Jensen Huang Returns & More
items.blurb: Sarvam Defends Token Factory Sarvam is standing its ground. Under fire for hosting Chinese AI models on its inference service,…
items.text: Sarvam is standing its ground. Under fire for hosting Chinese AI models on its inference service, the AI unicorn has clarified that it is creating a new commercial opportunity. The startup has also reiterated plans to double down on indigenous LLMs. Sarvam Hits Back: Pushing back against criticism that Token Factory relies on taxpayer’s money to host models like DeepSeek and Kimi, Sarvam said that the offering relies strictly on privately procured GPUs. The startup said it received no direct cash payouts under IndiaAI Mission, and subsidies ended in March and only came in the form of subsidised hardware. The Case For Inference: Cofounder Pratyush Kumar said that most of India’s current token demand is served by overseas players. As per him, building domestic inference capacity could reduce this dependence and help local enterprises address issues like higher latency and data residency. He also said that inference is creating a new commercial business for Sarvam, which will generate vital revenue for funding its capex-intensive AI development.
